source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record Cholera in 1974 annual notification table
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1974-01-01..1974-12-31. Source states: 'Table l. Cases of Cholera Notified to WHO, 1974'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record annual cholera article for 1974, published 18 July 1975. The African section of the notification table lists only: Algeria, Angola, Cameroon, Cape Verde Islands, Chad, Dahomey, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Niger, Nigeria, South Africa, Southern Rhodesia, United Republic of Tanzania, Togo and Upper Volta (Africa total 7877 cases). Uganda does not appear, i.e. Uganda notified zero cholera cases to WHO for 1974. Control validation of this method: Uganda appears by name in the African section of the same WER annual notification tables for every year it did notify - 1975 (3 cases), 1978 (1120), 1980 (1539), 1987 (140) and 1991 (279 cases and 28 deaths) - so its absence from this year's table is a positive signal of zero notification rather than a text-extraction artefact. Corroboration: Wamala et al. 2013 PLOS NTD state that 'During the subsequent years up to 1993, Uganda reported cholera cases every 2-4 years', describing an episodic epidemic pattern with genuinely quiet intervals. CAVEAT: classified Inferred_Absence rather than Documented_Absence and weighted 0.7 because zero notification under the International Health Regulations is not identical to zero transmission; the WER annual articles of this era themselves warn that there is 'strong reason to believe that cholera is present in a number of countries which have not notified cases in accordance with the International Health Regulations'. Country context: Uganda was under the Amin government in this period and its health system was severely degraded, so under-ascertainment is plausible. However Uganda did notify cholera to WHO in 1975 (3 cases), 1978 (1120), 1979 (940) and 1980 (1539), so the WHO notification channel itself was functioning on either side of this interval.

source: Cummings et al. 2012 Epidemiol Infect: A cholera outbreak among semi-nomadic pastoralists in northeastern Uganda
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1998-01-01..2010-04-20. Source states: 'Prior to April 2010, when a cholera outbreak emerged in Karamoja, the region had not reported cases of the disease since 1997'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. SUB-NATIONAL absence, Karamoja sub-region, from the peer-reviewed investigation of the April-July 2010 Karamoja outbreak (Cummings et al. 2012 Epidemiol Infect 140(8):1376-1385). The paper names the seven Karamoja districts as Kotido, Nakapiripirit, Abim, Amudat, Napak, Kaabong and Moroto; Amudat, Napak (both 2010), Abim (2006), Kaabong (2005) and Nabilatuk (2017) were carved out of Moroto, Kotido and Nakapiripirit during or after the absence period, so the absence is recorded against the three parent districts that existed throughout and geographically covered the whole sub-region. Labelled Inferred_Absence, NOT Documented_Absence: the source's wording is 'had not reported cases', which is a statement about the notification record rather than an affirmative finding of absence, and Karamoja was under recurrent insecurity (cattle raiding and the 2001-2010 forced disarmament) with the weakest health infrastructure in Uganda, hence surveillance status partial. Supporting context from the same paper: 'information regarding epidemiological trends and location-specific risk factors was not readily available' because of the extended time between outbreaks. This is a SUB-NATIONAL row only; Uganda as a whole reported cholera nationally in every year of 1998-2010, so this row must never be read as a national zero. py/build_weekly_timeseries.py uses national rows only for Uganda, which has ample national coverage, so these rows cannot leak into the national series.
